lavashak.name: Lavashak
lavashak.summary: An ancient Iranian sweet-and-sour fruit leather made from dried purees such as plum, apricot or pomegranate, once prepared only at home.

kateh.name: Kateh
kateh.summary: A simple, sticky Iranian rice dish from the Caspian region, cooked faster than polo-style rice and often called Iran's 'everyday rice.'

gilan-province.name: Gilan province
gilan-province.summary: A province in northwestern Iran along the Caspian Sea, whose capital is the city of Rasht.

pilaf.name: Pilaf
pilaf.summary: A rice or wheat dish cooked in stock with spices and other ingredients, spread widely from the Abbasid Caliphate and known regionally as pilov, polow, pulao or paella.

lavash.name: Lavash
lavash.summary: A thin flatbread baked in a tandoor or on a griddle, a staple food in Armenia, eastern Georgia and parts of Iran.

caspian-kutum.name: Caspian kutum
caspian-kutum.summary: A medium-sized fish native to the Caspian Sea and its tributaries, once heavily harvested but now declined from overfishing and pollution; its flesh and roe are prized in Iran.

reshteh-khoshkar.name: Reshteh khoshkar
reshteh-khoshkar.summary: A traditional Ramadan cookie from Gilan Province, Iran, made of fried, patterned rice-flour pastry filled with sugar and crushed walnuts or hazelnuts.

parsian-esteghlal-international-hotel.name: Esteghlal Hotel
parsian-esteghlal-international-hotel.summary: A hotel in Tehran opened in 1962 as the Royal Tehran Hilton, designed by the Iranian architect Heydar Ghiai during the Pahlavi era.

pahlavi-dynasty.name: Pahlavi dynasty
pahlavi-dynasty.summary: The last royal dynasty to rule Iran, founded in 1925 by Reza Shah Pahlavi and overthrown in the 1979 Iranian Revolution.

heydar-ghiai.name: Heydar Ghiai
heydar-ghiai.summary: Iranian architect and university professor (1922–1985), an early figure in Iran's modern architectural movement who taught at the University of Tehran; best known for designing the Senate House of Iran.

art-of-persia-tv-series.name: Art of Persia
art-of-persia-tv-series.summary: A three-part 2020 BBC documentary series about the history and culture of Iran, presented by Samira Ahmed.

samira-ahmed.name: Samira Ahmed
samira-ahmed.summary: A British journalist and broadcaster for the BBC, presenting programmes such as Front Row and Newswatch, and the 2020 documentary Art of Persia.

persian-famine-of-1917-1919.name: Persian famine of 1917–1919
persian-famine-of-1917-1919.summary: A period of mass starvation and disease in occupied, officially neutral Iran during World War I, killing an estimated 2 million people from hunger, cholera, typhus and influenza.

armistice-of-mudros.name: Armistice of Mudros
armistice-of-mudros.summary: Agreement signed on 30 October 1918 ending hostilities between the Ottoman Empire and the Allies in the Middle Eastern theatre of World War I, leading to Allied occupation and the partition of Ottoman territory.

iran-iraq-war.name: Iran-Iraq War
iran-iraq-war.summary: A war beginning with Iraq's invasion of Iran in September 1980 that lasted eight years, caused around 500,000 deaths, and ended with a UN-brokered ceasefire in 1988.

harald-hjalmarson.name: Harald Hjalmarson
harald-hjalmarson.summary: Swedish military officer (1868–1919) who served in Iran's Gendarmerie during the First World War, then joined Finland's White Guard, where he proved an unpopular commander.

azerbaijan-iran.name: Iranian Azerbaijan
azerbaijan-iran.summary: A historical region in northwestern Iran, populated mainly by Azerbaijanis along with Kurdish, Armenian and other minorities, distinct from the neighboring Republic of Azerbaijan.

agha-petros.name: Agha Petros
agha-petros.summary: An Assyrian military leader (1880–1932) who commanded Assyrian and Armenian forces against Ottoman, Kurdish, and Qajar armies during World War I.

reza-shah.name: Reza Shah
reza-shah.summary: Shah of Iran from 1925 to 1941 and founder of the Pahlavi dynasty, who rose from army officer to seize power in a 1921 coup before being elected monarch.

persian-cossack-brigade.name: Persian Cossack Brigade
persian-cossack-brigade.summary: A Russian-modelled cavalry unit formed in Iran in 1879, commanded by Russian officers until 1920; it later helped bring Reza Shah to power and found the Pahlavi dynasty.

kazerun.name: Kazerun
kazerun.summary: A historic city in Fars Province, Iran, founded by Persians who fled the nearby Sasanian city of Bishapur after its destruction by Arab conquerors.

battle-of-robat-karim.name: Battle of Robat Karim
battle-of-robat-karim.summary: A World War I battle fought near Tehran between Iranian forces under Heydar Latifiyan and occupying Russian troops; the Russians won, but Iran avoided becoming a colony of any power during the war.

battle-of-shekar-yazi.name: Battle of Shekar Yazi
battle-of-shekar-yazi.summary: A 1920 clash in which the Kurdish leader Simko Shikak's forces fought the Iranian government, part of early 20th-century Kurdish uprisings in Iran seeking greater autonomy.

simko-shikak.name: Simko Shikak
simko-shikak.summary: Kurdish chieftain and warlord (1887–1930) who led thousands of rebels against Qajar and Pahlavi forces before being assassinated by the Iranian government.

amar-khan-shikak.name: Amar Khan Shikak
amar-khan-shikak.summary: A Kurdish tribal leader of the Shekak tribe, born 1873, who served as Simko Shikak's chief aide and led the tribe after Simko's assassination, later aligning with the Republic of Mahabad.

amir-arshad.name: Amir Arshad
amir-arshad.summary: An early 20th-century tribal military commander in Arasbaran, Iran, who supported the Constitutionalists and effectively ruled the region from 1911 to 1920 before being killed in battle.

qazvin.name: Qazvin
qazvin.summary: A city in northwestern Iran that served as capital of the Safavid Empire from 1555 to 1598 and is known today as Iran's calligraphy capital.

shahrbani.name: Shahrbani
shahrbani.summary: Iran's city police force, founded during the Qajar era and eventually merged in 1991 into what became the Islamic Republic's police command.

amin-maalouf.name: Amin Maalouf
amin-maalouf.summary: A Lebanese French author, born 1949, who writes in French though Arabic is his native language; his works include The Crusades Through Arab Eyes and the Goncourt-winning The Rock of Tanios.

omar-khayyam.name: Omar Khayyam
omar-khayyam.summary: Persian polymath (1048–1131) who advanced mathematics and astronomy, designed the precise Jalali solar calendar, and is traditionally credited with quatrain poetry.

rubaiyat-of-omar-khayyam.name: Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam
rubaiyat-of-omar-khayyam.summary: An 1859 English translation by Edward FitzGerald of quatrains attributed to Omar Khayyam, which became hugely popular from the 1880s and inspired 'Omar Khayyam clubs.'

nizam-al-mulk.name: Nizam al-Mulk
nizam-al-mulk.summary: Persian scholar and vizier of the Seljuk Empire (1018-1092) who became its de facto ruler for 20 years and founded a network of madrasas called the Nizamiyyas.

hasan-i-sabbah.name: Hasan-i Sabbah
hasan-i-sabbah.summary: Founder of the Nizari Ismaili sect and the Order of Assassins, who ruled the Nizari Ismaili state from the fortress of Alamut from 1090 to his death in 1124.

jordan-mechner.name: Jordan Mechner
jordan-mechner.summary: American video game designer who created the 1984 game Karateka and the 1989 hit Prince of Persia, both using rotoscoped animation.

prince-of-persia-1989-video-game.name: Prince of Persia (1989)
prince-of-persia-1989-video-game.summary: A 1989 cinematic platform video game set in medieval Persia, in which the player must defeat the Grand Vizier Jaffar to save a princess; it launched a long-running franchise.

shahnameh.name: Shahnameh
shahnameh.summary: An epic poem of about 50,000 couplets written by the Persian poet Ferdowsi between around 977 and 1010 CE, telling Iran's mythical and historical past up to the Muslim conquest. It is regarded as Iran's national epic.

persian-constitutional-revolution.name: Persian Constitutional Revolution
persian-constitutional-revolution.summary: A 1905 to 1911 movement in Qajar Iran that established the country's first parliament, opening the way to a modern era of press debate and constitutional government.

abolqasem-lahouti.name: Lahouti
abolqasem-lahouti.summary: Iranian-Soviet poet and political activist (1887–1957), active during Iran's Constitutional Revolution and later in Tajikistan during the early Soviet era.

mohammad-farrokhi-yazdi.name: Farrokhi Yazdi
mohammad-farrokhi-yazdi.summary: Iranian poet, journalist and senior politician (1889–1939) known as the "Crown of poets," active during the Persian Constitutional Revolution and the Reza Pahlavi era.

ahmad-shamlou.name: Ahmad Shamlou
ahmad-shamlou.summary: Iranian poet, writer and journalist who lived from 1925 to 2000 and is regarded as the most influential Persian poet of modern Iran after Nima Yooshij.

ahmed-rashid.name: Ahmed Rashid
ahmed-rashid.summary: Pakistani journalist, born 1948, and best-selling author of books about Afghanistan, Pakistan and Central Asia.

national-consultative-assembly.name: Majles (National Consultative Assembly)
national-consultative-assembly.summary: Iran's national legislative body from 1906 to 1979, established by the Persian Constitution of 1906 and elected by universal suffrage, later including women after 1963.

qajar-dynasty.name: Qajar dynasty
qajar-dynasty.summary: An Iranian ruling family that gained prominence in the 16th century and governed Iran from 1789 to 1925, ending when Reza Shah was declared the new shah.

pahlavi-iran.name: Imperial State of Persia
pahlavi-iran.summary: The Western name, until 1935, for the Iranian state ruled by the Pahlavi dynasty from 1925 to 1979.

ruhollah-khomeini.name: Ruhollah Khomeini
ruhollah-khomeini.summary: Iranian cleric and politician (1900–1989) who led the Iranian Revolution that overthrew the shah and became Iran's first supreme leader, serving until his death.

1953-iranian-coup-d-tat.name: 1953 Iranian Coup
1953-iranian-coup-d-tat.summary: British- and American-backed coup on 19 August 1953 that overthrew Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh after he nationalized Iran's oil industry, strengthening the Shah's rule.

george-curzon-1st-marquess-curzon-of-ked.name: Lord Curzon
george-curzon-1st-marquess-curzon-of-ked.summary: British statesman and Conservative politician (1859–1925) who served as Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905 and Foreign Secretary from 1919 to 1924.
george-curzon-1st-marquess-curzon-of-ked.source_title: George Curzon, 1st Marquess Curzon of Kedleston

anglo-persian-oil-company.name: Anglo-Persian Oil Company
anglo-persian-oil-company.summary: A British company founded in 1909 after a major oil discovery in Persia; the British government took a controlling 51% stake in 1914, and it later became British Petroleum.

william-morgan-shuster.name: William Morgan Shuster
william-morgan-shuster.summary: William Morgan Shuster: American lawyer and civil servant (1877–1960) best known as Treasurer-General of Persia, appointed by Iran's parliament in 1911, a post he held only until December that year.

mohammad-reza-pahlavi.name: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi
mohammad-reza-pahlavi.summary: Last Shah of Iran, reigning from 1941 to 1979, whose rule saw the 1953 coup against Mosaddegh and the 1963 White Revolution before he was overthrown in the Islamic Revolution.

shirin-ebadi.name: Shirin Ebadi
shirin-ebadi.summary: Iranian lawyer, judge and human rights activist (born 1947) who won the 2003 Nobel Peace Prize, the first Iranian to receive it, for her work on democracy and rights.

islamic-consultative-assembly.name: Islamic Consultative Assembly
islamic-consultative-assembly.summary: Iran's unicameral national legislative body, also called the Iranian Parliament or Majles, currently made up of 290 representatives.

ahmad-shah-qajar.name: Ahmad Shah Qajar
ahmad-shah-qajar.summary: Shah of Iran from 1909 to 1925 and the last ruler of the Qajar dynasty, who came to the throne at age 11 after his father was deposed by parliament.

baloch-people.name: Baloch people
baloch-people.summary: An ethnic group speaking Balochi, native to the Balochistan region across Pakistan, Iran and Afghanistan, traditionally nomadic pastoralists; most live in Pakistan.

bakhtiari-people.name: Bakhtiari
bakhtiari-people.summary: A Lur tribe from Iran, traditionally nomadic pastoralists who migrated between summer and winter pastures; concentrated today in Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari, Khuzestan, Lorestan, Bushehr and Isfahan provinces.

greater-and-lesser-tunbs.name: Tunb Islands
greater-and-lesser-tunbs.summary: Two small islands in the Persian Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz, administered by Iran but claimed by the United Arab Emirates.

hussein-ali-montazeri.name: Hussein-Ali Montazeri
hussein-ali-montazeri.summary: Iranian Grand Ayatollah (1922–2009) and reformist who was the only deputy supreme leader of Iran, from 1985 to 1989. He was a major leader of the Iranian Revolution and later a human rights advocate.

khaz-al-ibn-jabir.name: Sheikh Khazal
khaz-al-ibn-jabir.summary: Ruler of Arabistan and Sheikh of Mohammerah (1861–1936), head of the Kasebite clan of the Banu Ka'b and overlord of the Shatt al-Arab, regarded as one of the most powerful Arabian rulers of his time.

khosrow-bagheri.name: Khosrow Bagheri
khosrow-bagheri.summary: Iranian philosopher and educational theorist who serves as president of the Philosophy of Education Society of Iran.

mulla-sadra.name: Mulla Sadra
mulla-sadra.summary: Iranian Islamic philosopher, theologian and mystic (c. 1571/2 – c. 1635/40) who led Iran's 17th-century cultural renaissance and is considered by some the most influential Muslim philosopher of the last four centuries.

ludwig-wittgenstein.name: Ludwig Wittgenstein
ludwig-wittgenstein.summary: Austro-British philosopher (1889–1951) working in logic and philosophy of language, born into a wealthy Viennese family and educated under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge.

john-searle.name: John Searle
john-searle.summary: American philosopher (1932–2025) known for speech act theory and the 'Chinese room' argument against strong artificial intelligence.

saul-kripke.name: Saul Kripke
saul-kripke.summary: American philosopher and logician (1940–2022) known for his possible-worlds semantics for modal logic and his 1980 book Naming and Necessity, considered a major 20th-century philosophical work.

friedrich-nietzsche.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
friedrich-nietzsche.summary: A German philosopher and former classical philologist known for critiquing objective truth and Christian morality, who suffered a mental collapse in 1889.

martin-heidegger.name: Martin Heidegger
martin-heidegger.summary: German philosopher (1889–1976) central to phenomenology, hermeneutics and existentialism, whose 1927 book Being and Time is considered one of modern philosophy's most significant works.

ahmad-fardid.name: Ahmad Fardid
ahmad-fardid.summary: Iranian philosopher (1910–1994) and Tehran University professor, influenced by Martin Heidegger. He is considered one of the philosophical ideologues of the Islamic government that came to power in Iran in 1979.

gharbzadegi.name: Gharbzadegi
gharbzadegi.summary: Persian-origin term, often translated 'Westoxification', for the unquestioning imitation of Western ways, seen as a loss of Iranian cultural identity. It was first coined in the 1940s.

jalal-al-e-ahmad.name: Jalal Al-e-Ahmad
jalal-al-e-ahmad.summary: Iranian novelist, translator and social critic (1923–1969), regarded as one of the earliest prominent Iranian ethnographers. His critique of the West drew on themes from Frantz Fanon and Marx.

abdolkarim-soroush.name: Abdolkarim Soroush
abdolkarim-soroush.summary: Iranian Islamic scholar, born in 1945, and former philosophy professor at the University of Tehran. Time magazine named him one of the world's 100 most influential people in 2005.

martin-luther.name: Martin Luther
martin-luther.summary: German priest and theologian (1483–1546) who sparked the Protestant Reformation with his 1517 Ninety-five Theses and was excommunicated by the pope in 1521.

islamic-government.name: Islamic Government
islamic-government.summary: Book by Ayatollah Khomeini, first published in 1970 and perhaps the most influential modern document supporting theocratic rule. Its doctrine shaped the 1979 Constitution, which made Khomeini Iran's first Supreme Leader.

seyyed-hossein-nasr.name: Seyyed Hossein Nasr
seyyed-hossein-nasr.summary: Iranian-American philosopher and Islamic scholar born in 1933, who taught philosophy in Tehran before the 1979 Islamic Revolution forced him into exile in the United States.

farah-pahlavi.name: Farah Pahlavi
farah-pahlavi.summary: Last queen and empress of Iran, born in 1938, and widow of the last shah, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. She founded charities and Shiraz University, and left Iran with the Shah in January 1979.

iranian-research-institute-of-philosophy.name: Iranian Research Institute of Philosophy
iranian-research-institute-of-philosophy.summary: Public research institute in Tehran, Iran, known today as the Iranian Research Institute of Philosophy.

muhammad-husayn-tabataba-i.name: Muhammad Husayn Tabataba'i
muhammad-husayn-tabataba-i.summary: Iranian scholar and philosopher (1903-1981), among the most prominent thinkers of modern Shia Islam. Also known as Allameh Tabataba'i, he is best known for the Tafsir al-Mizan, a Quran commentary.

the-principles-of-philosophy-and-the-met.name: The Principles of Philosophy and the Method of Realism
the-principles-of-philosophy-and-the-met.summary: Book of 14 articles by Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai on Islamic philosophy and epistemology, published in five volumes. It also examines and critiques Western philosophy.
the-principles-of-philosophy-and-the-met.source_title: The Principles of Philosophy and the Method of Realism

morteza-motahhari.name: Morteza Motahhari
morteza-motahhari.summary: Iranian Shia scholar, philosopher and lecturer (1919-1979) who deeply influenced the ideology of the Islamic Republic. A disciple of Khomeini, he chaired the Council of the Islamic Revolution until his assassination.

tafsir-al-mizan.name: Tafsir al-Mizan
tafsir-al-mizan.summary: Commentary on the Quran written in Arabic by the Shia scholar and philosopher Muhammad Husayn Tabatabaei (1892–1981). It has been printed in several editions in Iran and Lebanon.

karl-popper.name: Karl Popper
karl-popper.summary: Austrian-British philosopher (1902-1994) known for rejecting inductivism in favor of falsifiability as the test of scientific theories, and for defending liberal democracy against totalitarianism.

al-farabi.name: Al-Farabi
al-farabi.summary: Early Islamic philosopher and music theorist (c. 870–950), called the "Second Master" after Aristotle. He is credited as the first Muslim to present philosophy as a coherent system and is known in the Latin West as Alpharabius.

nowruz.name: Nowruz
nowruz.summary: The Iranian New Year, marking the spring equinox and rooted in Zoroastrianism, celebrated for over 3,000 years across West and Central Asia, the Caucasus, and South Asia.

abbas-kiarostami.name: Abbas Kiarostami
abbas-kiarostami.summary: Iranian film director and poet (1940-2016) who won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 1997 for Taste of Cherry and is regarded as one of Iran's most influential filmmakers.

palme-d-or.name: Palme d'Or
palme-d-or.summary: The top prize awarded to the director of the best film at the Cannes Film Festival, introduced in 1955 and considered one of the film industry's most prestigious honors.

taste-of-cherry.name: Taste of Cherry
taste-of-cherry.summary: 1997 Iranian minimalist drama written, directed, and edited by Abbas Kiarostami, about a Tehran man seeking someone to bury him after his planned suicide. It won the Palme d'Or at Cannes that year.

guardianship-of-the-islamic-jurist.name: Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist
guardianship-of-the-islamic-jurist.summary: A Shia Islamic doctrine, developed by Ruhollah Khomeini, holding that religious jurists should govern society; it forms the basis of Iran's constitution.

ja-fari-school.name: Ja'fari school
ja-fari-school.summary: The largest school of Islamic jurisprudence in Shia Islam, founded on the teachings of the sixth Shia Imam, Ja'far al-Sadiq.

ehsan-yarshater.name: Ehsan Yarshater
ehsan-yarshater.summary: Ehsan Yarshater: Iranian historian and linguist (1920–2018), founder and director of the Center for Iranian Studies at Columbia University and one of the editors of the Encyclopaedia Iranica.

mohammad-ali-foroughi.name: Mohammad Ali Foroughi
mohammad-ali-foroughi.summary: Iranian politician, writer and diplomat (1877–1942) who served three terms as prime minister, the first under Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, and founded the Academy of Iran.

asghar-farhadi.name: Asghar Farhadi
asghar-farhadi.summary: An Iranian film director and screenwriter known for intimate family dramas, winner of two Academy Awards for A Separation and The Salesman.

a-separation.name: A Separation
a-separation.summary: A 2011 Iranian drama film directed by Asghar Farhadi, the first Iranian film to win the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film and the Berlin Film Festival's Golden Bear.

the-salesman-2016-film.name: The Salesman
the-salesman-2016-film.summary: 2016 Iranian-French drama film written and directed by Asghar Farhadi, which won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film and two awards at Cannes.

1974-asian-games.name: 1974 Asian Games
1974-asian-games.summary: Games held in Tehran in September 1974, the first time the Asian Games were hosted in the Middle East, drawing 3,010 athletes from 25 nations.

haile-selassie.name: Haile Selassie
haile-selassie.summary: Emperor of Ethiopia from 1930 to 1974, born Tafari Makonnen; he introduced modernizing reforms, led Ethiopia through Italian occupation, and is revered as divine in Rastafari.

hussein-of-jordan.name: Hussein of Jordan
hussein-of-jordan.summary: King of Jordan from 1952 until his death in 1999, a Hashemite monarch who led the country through three wars with Israel.

neil-armstrong.name: Neil Armstrong
neil-armstrong.summary: American astronaut and commander of Apollo 11, who in 1969 became the first person to walk on the Moon; also a naval aviator and test pilot.

buzz-aldrin.name: Buzz Aldrin
buzz-aldrin.summary: The second person to walk on the Moon, as Lunar Module pilot on Apollo 11 in July 1969, and a former US Air Force fighter pilot.

michael-collins-astronaut.name: Michael Collins
michael-collins-astronaut.summary: An American astronaut (1930–2021) who piloted the Apollo 11 command module in lunar orbit in 1969 while Armstrong and Aldrin made the first Moon landing.

ashkan-rahgozar.name: Ashkan Rahgozar
ashkan-rahgozar.summary: An Iranian animation director and filmmaker, born in 1986, and founder of Hoorakhsh Studios.

the-last-fiction.name: The Last Fiction
the-last-fiction.summary: A 2020 Iranian animated film by Ashkan Rahgozar retelling the Shahnameh tale of Zahhak, the first Iranian animated film in Academy Awards competition.
